variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A knowledge graph represents facts as entities and named relationships. Instead of storing only a paragraph that says "Atlas depends on Token Service," the graph stores Atlas, Token Service, and a directed DEPENDS_ON edge between them.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Entity
pairs.detail: A stable identity such as employee EMP-104, service svc-token, or paper doi:10.1234/example.
pairs.explanation: A stable identity such as employee EMP-104, service svc-token, or paper doi:10.1234/example. Names are attributes, not durable identifiers.

pairs.label: Relationship
pairs.detail: A typed, directed claim such as WORKS_ON, DEPENDS_ON, or CITES.
pairs.explanation: A typed, directed claim such as WORKS_ON, DEPENDS_ON, or CITES. Direction and meaning must be explicit.

pairs.label: Schema
pairs.detail: Entity types, relation types, required properties, and constraints keep accidental strings from becoming arbitrary graph structure.
pairs.explanation: Entity types, relation types, required properties, and constraints keep accidental strings from becoming arbitrary graph structure.

pairs.label: Provenance
pairs.detail: Source records, extraction versions, confidence, timestamps, and permissions let the system verify or withdraw a claim.
pairs.explanation: Source records, extraction versions, confidence, timestamps, and permissions let the system verify or withdraw a claim.

variants.prompt: What is the core trust invariant of a production knowledge graph?
options: Every node must have a human-readable name.
Every accepted node and edge remains traceable to evidence, policy, and time.
Every query must traverse at least three hops.
